preferred_themes: memory and the reconstruction of the past
roads not taken / what might have been
moral proximity to horror and complicity
summary: This is someone who wants to sit inside a single feeling for two hours — quiet, memory-soaked dramas about grief, longing, and the lives we didn't live (Aftersun, Past Lives, Roma) are dead center for them, and they'll follow an art-house film into genuine discomfort as long as the emotion is honest (The Zone of Interest). The 'liked' tier (Drive My Car, Nomadland, Anatomy of a Fall) shows they still value restraint and interiority but cool slightly when a film gets more procedural or diffuse. Kinetic action leaves them completely cold — anything built on spectacle, revenge, or a dozen things happening at once is a hard pass. Recommend something slow, aching, and formally assured, ideally international, and don't worry about giving it a happy ending.
